title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 142
paragraphs: This seemed to them, as indeed it was, a milder utterance than the first. So they had it written down and departed with it to Athens. When the messengers on their return reported to the people, many differing opinions were expressed by those who tried to interpret the oracle, and among them these, standing most at odds with one another: some of the older men said that they thought the god had prophesied that the Acropolis would survive, for the Acropolis of the Athenians had in old times been fenced with a thorn hedge, and they took the phrase “wall of wood” to refer to this hedge. Others, on the contrary, said that the god meant their ships by this, and they advised leaving everything else aside and getting these ready. Those who claimed the ships were the wall of wood were, however, shaken in their interpretation by the last two verses the priestess uttered:
“Salamis, thou divine, thou shalt bring sons of women to perish, either when grain is sown or when it is gathered in.”

On these verses the opinion of those who said that the ships were the wall of wood was disturbed, for the professional interpreters of oracles took these to mean that they were fated, if they prepared for a sea-battle, to be defeated around Salamis.
